Aalto University is a multidisciplinary research university in Espoo, Finland. It was formed in 2010 by merging three Finnish universities: the Helsinki School of Economics, the Helsinki University of Technology, and the Helsinki University of Art and Design. Aalto University provides Bachelor's, Master's, and Doctoral degree programs in subjects such as business, engineering, arts and design, and science. The university is well-known for emphasizing entrepreneurship, sustainability, and innovation. With students from over 100 countries, Aalto University boasts a varied and international student body. The institution also includes various research facilities and is dedicated to research and innovation. As Collab International, we will give you all the information to inform you.

Aalto University provides a number of study-abroad options for overseas students who want to spend a semester or a year at the university. The institution has over 400 university collaborations globally, and students can pick from various courses in business, engineering, science, arts, and design. Aalto University has two significant study abroad programs: Erasmus+ and Aalto Partner Program. The Erasmus+ program is open to students from European Union member nations and provides money and support for one or two semesters of study at Aalto University. The Aalto Partner Program is offered to non-EU students. It permits them to study at Aalto University for one or two semesters, possibly earning credits toward their home university degree. Aside from these programs, Aalto University provides a number of summer school programs for international students who desire to study in Finland during the summer. Summer school programs provide a variety of courses in business, engineering, science, and design.

Aalto University provides a variety of postgraduate programs in a variety of subjects, each with its own set of admission requirements. Applicants must have a relevant bachelor's degree, exhibit English language proficiency, and provide a range of application papers, including transcripts, a CV, a motivation letter, letters of recommendation, proof of language proficiency, and a passport or ID.
